_comment: Pairwise accuracy for the preference reward model and its comparison points, on one split under one harness. Written so the baseline number stops living only in prose: every figure below is reproducible with the command recorded against it.

openassistant_deberta_v3_large_v2.note: Re-run on CPU to produce this artifact after an audit found the figure existed only in prose. It reproduced the published 0.6009 exactly.

ours_lr5e5_collapsed_run.note: A learning-rate sweep failure, retained as the reference point for what a collapsed run looks like on this split.

reading: The 10.2-point gap is in-distribution for our model and out-of-distribution for the baseline, so it is not a claim that a 184M model is better than a 435M one in general. It says the smaller model fits this preference distribution better than a strong public model transfers onto it. The out-of-distribution counterpart to this number is in rewardbench2_results.json, where our unweighted six-domain average is 25.3 -- the random floor.
